claim: durable population-scale therapy/health raises marriageability and clears the E21 null
evidence: durable best +0.140 (bends) vs the E21 voluntary-program null; it enters through marriageability q, a different channel from relationship-repair

claim: voluntary one-off couples therapy stays null
evidence: voluntary best +0.013 - q rises then erodes back (BSF/SHM/Army-PREP fade); confirms E21 in-model

claim: marriageability is bilateral - alienation lowers it for men AND women
evidence: q gates coupling for the population, not one sex; a fall in q reduces partnership formation regardless of side - un-marriageable men and women together

claim: father-access loss has no contemporary effect but a delayed intergenerational cost
evidence: father-access -0.4 (Germany): +0.000 at 2045 (contemporary ~0) but -0.111 by 2095 - the one-generation lag of the childhood-env path integral

claim: the intergenerational alienation compounds over the horizon
evidence: the loss deepens +0.000@2045 → -0.189@2124; the per-cohort path integral accumulates, so the cost grows rather than plateauing - a spiral

claim: relationship scars impose a delayed next-generation coupling cost
evidence: a scar forcing lowers childhood env → next-cohort q → coupling with the same one-generation delay; Germany ΔTFR -0.149 by 2125

claim: a shared-custody presumption pays a delayed intergenerational dividend
evidence: custody (coupling insurance + father investment) gives +0.128 at 2050 rising to +0.259 at 2110 - the E24-H180 lever earns a second, delayed payoff through the child cohort

claim: paternity certainty raises father investment and pays an intergenerational dividend
evidence: father-access GAIN +0.4 lifts the next cohort's marriageability, +0.141 by 2110 - the mirror of the alienation loss

claim: the therapy dividend also compounds intergenerationally
evidence: durable therapy raises q, which raises father investment (phi*q) → childhood env → the next cohort's q - a healthier-fathers second dividend on top of the contemporary lift

claim: the intergenerational channel is calibrated to the fatherlessness literature
evidence: the father-absence path integral is register-backed (McLanahan-Sandefur; Autor 2019) and bounded rather than point-fit; the delay (27-45yr) and childhood window (0-18) are demographic, not tuned

the shared-custody lever's benefit grows ~2.0x from 2050 (+0.128) to 2110 (+0.259) as the intergenerational dividend lands on top of its contemporary effect; a 2050-horizon evaluation captures only about half its eventual worth

claim: alienation is hysteresis-adjacent - a lost generation propagates forward
evidence: because a cohort's low q feeds the next cohort's childhood env, a depressed generation transmits forward; the loss at -0.189@2124 is still deepening, not recovering, within the horizon

a security push (fS=0.20) leaves q unmoved (qend +0.0000) while raising TFR only through the security channel; marriageability is health/attachment, not income - cash and marriageability are not substitutes

claim: the intergenerational memory reframes the campaign - score levers over two generations
evidence: the delayed dividends (custody, therapy, paternity) and the compounding costs (alienation, scars) only appear on a multi-generation horizon; a single-generation ledger misprices every structural lever
